situation: Matched with a girl on Hinge. Her profile says she ran the Tokyo marathon, and one prompt is 'my most irrational fear: ramen that isn't hot enough'.
reply: Important question: after the Tokyo marathon, was the reward ramen at a dangerous temperature, or was that too much after 42km?
note: Ties her two details together into one easy, specific question, and says nothing about you or her looks.

situation: 想从产品运营转做用户研究。在领英上看到一位在字节做UX研究的前辈陈然，她写过一篇讲可用性测试样本量的文章，想私信请教一个问题。
reply: 陈然您好，读了您那篇《5个用户够不够》，第一次把样本量这件事讲明白了，我们团队上周就照着做了两轮小样本测试。我正在从产品运营转做用户研究，想请教一个具体问题：您是怎么判断一轮测试可以在第几个用户停下来的？方便的话回我两句就很感谢，没空也完全理解。
note: 先证明你认真读过她的东西，再问一个两句话能答完的问题，不约电话。

situation: I DMed a woodworker on Instagram asking what finish he uses on his walnut tables. He just replied 'Rubio Monocoat' and nothing else.
reply: Perfect, thank you. Ordering a tin for my first walnut side table this weekend.
note: A curt answer to your question is a win. Thank him in one line and don't ask for more.

situation: I emailed a researcher I don't know, Dr. Ines Alvarez, on Sept 21 asking one quick question about her public urban heat dataset. No reply after 8 days. Is one follow-up okay?
reply: Hi Dr. Alvarez, bumping this once in case it got lost in the start of term. The question is only whether the 2023 sensor readings in your heat-island dataset are hourly or daily averages. No worries at all if you're not able to reply.
note: One follow-up, with the question restated so she can answer without scrolling back. If this gets no reply, stop.

situation: Hice match en Bumble con Lucía. En una foto sale con un galgo y en su perfil dice que es de Cádiz y que "el mejor pescaíto frito no está en Cádiz", sin decir dónde.
reply: Vale, me has dejado con la intriga: si el mejor pescaíto frito no está en Cádiz, ¿dónde está? Y el galgo, ¿opina lo mismo?
note: Una pregunta concreta sobre algo que ella misma dejó abierto, fácil de responder y sin hablar de su físico.

situation: My 6-year-old keeps talking about a boy in her class, Oscar, they play dinosaurs every break. I don't know his parents. The class WhatsApp shows his mum is Hannah. I'd like to suggest a playdate.
reply: Hi Hannah, I'm Kate, Zoe's mum from Class 1B. Zoe comes home every day with a new story about her and Oscar running the dinosaur park at break; apparently he's the T. rex expert. Would Oscar like to come to ours after school one day next week? Wednesday or Thursday would work, and I'm happy to do the pickup.
note: Proof you looked is the kids' own story; the ask is small, concrete and easy to decline.

situation: Just moved to Leeds and found a board game group on Meetup. The organiser, Tom, posted about a Wingspan night on Thursday Oct 8. I've never been to one of these and want to message him first.
reply: Hi Tom, saw the Wingspan night on Thursday the 8th. I've played it twice and still end up with a sad little handful of birds. Is it fine to turn up as a fairly new player, or is that night more for regulars?
note: Community first contact: one detail from his post, one clause about you, one question he can answer in a line.

situation: 上周六在北京参加了一场播客线下分享会，嘉宾苏晴讲了怎么从听众来信里挑选题，我觉得特别好，但当天没来得及跟她聊。我自己也在做一个小播客，想在小红书私信她。
reply: 苏晴你好，上周六在三里屯那场播客分享会上听了你讲怎么从听众来信里挑选题，那是我当天笔记记得最多的一段。我自己在做一个聊城市散步的小播客，想请教一个具体问题：来信那么多，你是按什么标准判断哪一封能做成一期的？方便的话回我一两句就很感谢，没空也完全理解。
note: 活动后的第一条私信：先说清在哪儿见过、记住了她讲的哪一点，再问一个一两句就能答完的问题，不约电话。

situation: Matched with Sam on Hinge. His profile is almost empty: one photo of him holding a cello in what looks like a kitchen, and the only prompt answer is 'ask me'. No idea what to open with.
reply: You said ask, so: is the cello a serious thing, or a kitchen concert for one? Secretly hoping for the second.
note: With a near-empty profile, use the one detail there is and make the answer easy. No compliment on looks, no ask.

situation: I DMed a woman on our city's climbing Discord to thank her for her beta on a V5 at the gym, then asked if she wanted to climb together sometime. She replied that she's only there to talk climbing and finds DMs from strangers asking to meet up uncomfortable.
reply: Sorry, that was out of line. I'll leave you be.
note: When they say it wasn't welcome: one line of apology, no explanation, and no further messages.

situation: 我在HelloTalk上找日语语伴。看到一个在学中文的日本女生，资料里写上个月刚爬完富士山，还说《龙猫》看了二十遍。想发第一条消息。
reply: 你好！看到你上个月刚爬完富士山，还有《龙猫》看了二十遍，这个次数我服了。我也是宫崎骏迷，正在学日语。想问问：你爬富士山是半夜出发去山顶看日出的那种吗？
note: 语伴也是陌生人：接住资料里的一个具体细节，问一个好回答的问题，先不急着约练习时间。

situation: 我是杭州的自由插画师。小红书上关注了一家新开的咖啡馆'慢岛'，老板发帖说豆子都是自己去云南保山挑的，但店里的菜单还是打印的表格。想私信问问他们有没有兴趣做一版手绘菜单。
reply: 你好！看了你们去保山挑豆子那篇，最喜欢在咖啡园里晒豆的那张照片。我是杭州的插画师，平时常给小店画菜单和包装，想问一句：店里的菜单有考虑过做一版手绘的吗？有兴趣的话我发三张以前的作品给你看，没有也完全理解。
note: 陌生的生意私信：先证明认真看过对方的内容，自我介绍一句，只问一个好回答的小问题，第一条不报价。

situation: Matched with a guy on Tinder and he opened with just 'hey'. His profile says he's a firefighter and his photos are mostly bowls he's made on a pottery wheel. I want to reply with something better than 'hey' back.
reply: Hey! A firefighter whose hobby involves a 1,200-degree kiln feels like a busman's holiday. What got you into pottery?
note: When they open with 'hey', don't mirror it: pick up one detail and hand them an easy question.

situation: AncestryDNA matched me as a likely second cousin with Margaret Kelly in Cork. Her public tree has a Bridget Doyle born 1911 in Kilkenny, and my great-grandmother Nora Doyle was born there in 1908. I'm in Boston and want to message her through the site.
reply: Hi Margaret, Ancestry lists us as likely second cousins, and I think I can see why: your tree has Bridget Doyle, born 1911 in Kilkenny, and my great-grandmother was Nora Doyle, born there in 1908. Do you know if Bridget ever mentioned a sister who went to Boston? No pressure at all if you'd rather not dig into it.
note: A DNA match is still a stranger: one specific link from her tree, one easy question, and room not to reply.

situation: We bought a 1920s house in Asheville this summer. Clearing the attic we found a box of old letters and photos addressed to the Whitfield family. A neighbour says the daughter, Carol Whitfield, now lives in Ohio and gave me her email.
reply: Hi Carol, my husband and I bought 212 Elm Street in Asheville this summer, and I believe it was your family's home. Clearing the attic, we found a small box of letters and photos addressed to the Whitfields, including one of a girl on the porch swing dated 1961. Would you like them? I'd be glad to post them to you, no cost and no rush.
note: Lead with the one detail that proves the connection, then a yes-or-no question that asks nothing of her.

situation: Found a room in a shared house on Cowley Road in Oxford, £720 a month. The poster, Priya, says she's a nurse on night shifts, wants a quiet housemate, and has a very spoiled cat called Mango. She mentions she's had loads of messages. I work 9 to 5 in a library and I'm a quiet homebody.
reply: Hi Priya, a quiet housemate around night shifts is something I can genuinely offer: I work 9 to 5 in a library and spend most evenings reading rather than hosting. I'm also firmly pro spoiled cats, so Mango's standards are safe with me. Could I come and see the room this Saturday, 3 October, at whatever time fits your sleep?
note: A listing with a crowded inbox: answer the things she asked for, show you read the details, and make one small ask.
